dialogues.speaker: Koyomi
dialogues.jp:
「じゃあ、今日から卒業パーティーの準備に入
　るけど、なるべく出席するんだよ」
dialogues.en:
"We're going to get ready for the graduation party. I hope
everybody will join in."
dialogues.text:
"We're going to get ready for the graduation party. I hope
everybody will join in."

dialogues.jp:
暦先生はそう言うと、出席簿片手に教室を出て
行く。
dialogues.en:
After Koyomi-sensei says that, she leaves the classroom with
an attendance book in her hands.
dialogues.text:
After Koyomi-sensei says that, she leaves the classroom with
an attendance book in her hands.

dialogues.jp: 「卒業パーティーか……」
dialogues.en: "Graduation party..."
dialogues.text: "Graduation party..."

dialogues.jp:
まったく、うちの学園も祭り好きだよな……ク
リスマスパーティーなんてのもあったし。
dialogues.en: We like parties, don't we? We had a Christmas party, too.
dialogues.text: We like parties, don't we? We had a Christmas party, too.

dialogues.jp:
なにも卒業式の後に、パーティーなんてしなく
てもいいのにな。
dialogues.en:
I don't know why we have to have a party after the
graduation ceremony.
dialogues.text:
I don't know why we have to have a party after the
graduation ceremony.

dialogues.jp: （しかも、パーティーというより小さな学園祭）
dialogues.en: (It's more like a campus festival than a party.)
dialogues.text: (It's more like a campus festival than a party.)

dialogues.jp:
クラスや部活など関係なく、各人が好きな催し
物を企画できる。なんでもありの、創作発表の
場。
dialogues.en:
Anybody can plan their own event, and it can have nothing to
do with a class or club activity. There are many different
kinds of projects that anybody can show.
dialogues.text:
Anybody can plan their own event, and it can have nothing to
do with a class or club activity. There are many different
kinds of projects that anybody can show.

dialogues.jp:
しかも、催し物の企画に加わるかどうかは各人
の自由。なんの企画にも加わらず、純粋に客と
して参加することも出来る。
dialogues.en:
And it's up to you whether you want to participate in
planning the event or not.
dialogues.text:
And it's up to you whether you want to participate in
planning the event or not.

dialogues.jp:
こんな状況で進んで企画に参加するなんて、バ
カのすることだ。
dialogues.en:
In this situation, they must be idiots to participate in the
party.
dialogues.text:
In this situation, they must be idiots to participate in the
party.

dialogues.speaker: Suginami
dialogues.jp: 「パーティーがどうした、朝倉」
dialogues.en: "What about the party, Asakura?"
dialogues.text: "What about the party, Asakura?"

dialogues.jp:
やる気満々の顔をして、バカの頭領がやって来
る。
dialogues.en: A chief idiot comes by, brimming with eagerness.
dialogues.text: A chief idiot comes by, brimming with eagerness.

dialogues.jp: 「はりきってるな」
dialogues.en: "You look so excited."
dialogues.text: "You look so excited."

dialogues.speaker: Suginami
dialogues.jp: 「そう見えるか？」
dialogues.en: "Really?"
dialogues.text: "Really?"

dialogues.jp:
ニヤリと笑みを漏らすその表情は、誰が見ても、
腹黒さを感じるだろう。
dialogues.en:
The grin on his face would give anyone some kind of dark
thoughts.
dialogues.text:
The grin on his face would give anyone some kind of dark
thoughts.

dialogues.jp: 「また、何か｛・・／企画｝してるのか？」
dialogues.en: "Are you planning something?"
dialogues.text: "Are you planning something?"

dialogues.jp: いや、こいつがしてない訳ない。
dialogues.en: Of course he is. How can he not?
dialogues.text: Of course he is. How can he not?

dialogues.speaker: Suginami
dialogues.jp:
「フッ……付属最後を飾るに相応しいものを、
　現在進行中だ」
dialogues.en:
"Actually, I'm planning something to show appreciation for
this side school at the end."
dialogues.text:
"Actually, I'm planning something to show appreciation for
this side school at the end."

dialogues.jp: そうか、付属も遂に｛・・／最期｝を飾るのか……。
dialogues.en: I see. The side school will be at the end.
dialogues.text: I see. The side school will be at the end.

dialogues.jp: 「……捕まらんようにな」
dialogues.en: "Be careful not to get caught."
dialogues.text: "Be careful not to get caught."

dialogues.speaker: Suginami
dialogues.jp:
「心配はいらん。脱出ルートは既に確保してあ
　るからな」
dialogues.en: "Don't worry. I already secured the evacuation route."
dialogues.text: "Don't worry. I already secured the evacuation route."

dialogues.speaker: Suginami
dialogues.jp: 「……そうか」
dialogues.en: "I see."
dialogues.text: "I see."

dialogues.jp: どんなルートかはしらんが、多分｛・・／ダメ｝だろう。
dialogues.en:
I have no idea what kind of route it is, but it probably
won't work.
dialogues.text:
I have no idea what kind of route it is, but it probably
won't work.

dialogues.speaker: Suginami
dialogues.jp: 「おっと、そろそろ計画の第２段階に入らねば」
dialogues.en:
"Ooops, I'd better get going for the second stage of my
plan."
dialogues.text:
"Ooops, I'd better get going for the second stage of my
plan."

dialogues.jp: 教室を出て行く杉並を見送る。
dialogues.en: I bid Suginami farewell as he walks out of the classroom.
dialogues.text: I bid Suginami farewell as he walks out of the classroom.

dialogues.jp: ――あばよ友よ。
dialogues.en: See you, buddy.
dialogues.text: See you, buddy.

dialogues.jp: 「さて……俺もそろそろ行くか」
dialogues.en: "Well, I'd better get going, too."
dialogues.text: "Well, I'd better get going, too."

dialogues.jp:
俺は席を立ち、大きく伸びをすると、鞄を片手
に教室の出口へと向かった。
dialogues.en:
I get out of my chair and walk toward the classroom door,
with my bag in one hand.
dialogues.text:
I get out of my chair and walk toward the classroom door,
with my bag in one hand.

dialogues.jp: ◆あばよ友よ◆
dialogues.en: ◆Goodbye, friend◆
dialogues.text: ◆Goodbye, friend◆

dialogues.jp:
今日から卒パの準備期間に入る。企画に関して
は完全自由参加の卒パ。もちろん俺は参加しな
い予定だ。
dialogues.en:
We start the preparation for the graduation party from
today. Everyone can choose whether to participate or not. Of
course, I have no intention of doing so.
dialogues.text:
We start the preparation for the graduation party from
today. Everyone can choose whether to participate or not. Of
course, I have no intention of doing so.

dialogues.jp: もっとも、杉並はやる気まんまんのようだが。
dialogues.en: Of course, Suginami shows a great eagerness to do so.
dialogues.text: Of course, Suginami shows a great eagerness to do so.
